session.final_message:
I've built the Fernwheel site as `index.html` in your working folder. It's one file with inline CSS and JS, no build step, and the only external request is Google Fonts. I checked it in a headless browser at 1440px, 390px and 360px wide: there's no horizontal scrolling, no script errors, and the mobile menu, postcode check and form all behave as expected.

**What's on the page**
- **Hero:** "Ride more. Own less." beside an SVG e-bike with spinning wheels, plus key numbers (from €39/month, 48h replacement, €0 repairs) and a scrolling banner listing the benefits.
- **What's included:** insurance, repairs, 48h replacement and doorstep delivery.
- **How it works:** three steps.
- **Plans:** City €39, Plus €59 (marked "Most popular") and Cargo €89, each with its own SVG bike. Each plan's "Test ride" button fills that bike into the booking form and scrolls there.
- **Postcode check:** it works out the city from the postcode format, so 8004, 10437 and 1012 AB all work. In-area postcodes get a "Yes" with a link to book in that city. Nearby or out-of-area postcodes get a waitlist sign-up, and anything else gets a hint showing valid examples.
- **Test-ride form:** name, email, optional phone, city, date (tomorrow up to 60 days ahead), bike, time of day and a consent box. Errors show inline, and on success the form is replaced by a summary of the booking.
- **FAQ, a closing call to action and the footer.**
- **Phones and accessibility:** a menu button on narrow screens, large tap targets, keyboard focus outlines, screen-reader announcements for results, and reduced motion for visitors who've asked their device for it.

**Before you launch**
- **Nothing is sent anywhere yet.** The test-ride form and the waitlist only work in the browser. There's a `// TODO` in the form's submit handler where you'd send the booking to your server or a form service.
- **The delivery areas are my guesses:** Zurich 8001–8064, Berlin 10115–14199 and Amsterdam 1011–1109. They're set in the `lookup()` function, so change them to your real coverage.
- **I made up details you didn't give me:** the plan names, bike specs (range, cargo capacity), test ride length and hub locations, the FAQ answers, and the `hello@fernwheel.example` contact address. Prices are in € everywhere, including Zurich, so you may want to show CHF there.

I can also publish it as a private web page so you can share a link with your team.

session.final_message:
I've built the Fernwheel site as one file, `index.html` (about 91 KB). It has inline CSS and JS, Google Fonts (Bricolage Grotesque and Instrument Sans) and no images; the bike and icons are all SVG. I clicked through it on phone and desktop and it all works.

**What's on the page**
- **Hero:** a green e-bike drawn in SVG that rolls in once on load, with three labels showing what's included.
- **What's included:** the 48-hour replacement is the largest card, with a short timeline from reporting a problem to a new bike at the door.
- **How it works:** three numbered steps.
- **Plans:** Spark €39, Commute €59 (marked "Most popular") and Haul €89, with a strip below listing what every plan includes.
- **Postcode check:** works out the city from the postcode itself. Inputs like `d-10 997`, `1072ab` or `8004` all work. A match links straight to booking in that city. Postcodes outside your cities get a "notify me" email field instead. Unrecognised input shows an error explaining what to type.
- **Test-ride booking in two steps:**
  1. City, bike, day and time.
  2. Name, email and an optional phone number.

  It ends on a confirmation with an "Add to calendar" button that downloads a calendar file. City and bike are filled in from the postcode check or the plan you clicked, and unfinished choices are saved so visitors can come back to them.
- **FAQ, a closing call to action, the footer and a dark mode** that follows the device setting, with a toggle in the footer.

**Testing**
- I ran the full flow in a test browser: invalid, outside-area and valid postcodes, then the booking with errors on both steps, then a successful booking. There were no JavaScript errors.
- Checks at 360, 390 and 1440 px widths caught three real problems, all now fixed:
  - On phones the day picker pushed the booking section wider than the screen and cut off its text.
  - The postcode result overflowed its box at 360 px.
  - Some footer links were too small to tap.
- The automated design checks now flag only minor things I chose to keep:
  - The page uses 11 font sizes, mostly because of the large headline sizes.
  - The hero bike animation lasts 1.4 s, which is intentional.
  - The checker counts more than one orange button on the page. Each section has only one, and they all lead to the same booking.

**Design choices**
- "Book a free test ride" is the only orange (primary) button style. It's used for every booking button and appears once per section. Once a postcode matches, the "Check postcode" button turns grey so the next step stands out.
- On phones, a "Book a free test ride" bar stays at the bottom of the screen. It hides near the top of the page, at the booking form, at the closing call to action and when a postcode result is showing.
- Booking is split into two short steps with "Step 1 of 2" and a progress bar. Step 2 keeps a summary of the chosen ride with a "Change" link.
- Every form field has a visible label, errors appear next to the field with a fix, and the booking button is never disabled.
- Taps, hovers and keyboard focus all get visible feedback, the page works by keyboard, and animations are switched off for visitors who ask their device to reduce motion.

**Placeholder content you should confirm before launch.** I wrote these to fill the page; they aren't from your brief:
- Monthly cancellation with one month's notice, and the €0 deposit.
- Free delivery within about 3 working days.
- Bike specs and ranges for each plan.
- Zurich members paying the same numbers in Swiss francs (CHF 39 / 59 / 89).
- The postcode ranges for each city.
- The hub locations (Zurich Kreis 5, Berlin Kreuzberg, Amsterdam Oost) and the time slots.
- The email addresses and legal links in the footer.

The postcode check, booking and "notify me" form run entirely in the browser with a short fake delay, so nothing is sent anywhere yet. Hook them up to your booking system and CRM before launch.

If you want a private shareable link for your team, I can publish it as a page.
